title: Ella Beatty Appears in Ryan Murphy's New Series
seoTitle: Ella Beatty Stars in Ryan Murphy's Monster
subtitle: The actress brings the mysterious figure of Lizzie Borden to life in the latest installment of the Monster series
excerpt: The recently released Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story features Ella Beatty as Lizzie Borden, retelling the events of the 1892 Massachusetts case.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The release of the eighth season of the Monster series, titled Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, has brought actress Ella Beatty into the spotlight as she portrays Lizzie Borden, the central figure of the 1892 Massachusetts case. Written by Ian Brennan and directed by Max Winkler, the production blends historical facts with dramatic elements, generating widespread public interest.

What Changes in the Narrative with Ella Beatty

Ella Beatty takes on the role of Lizzie Borden, the 32-year-old woman accused of the murders of her father and stepmother. The series depicts the daily life of the Borden family, including the presence of Bridget Sullivan, the family maid, played by Vicky Krieps. The plot highlights the relationship between Lizzie and Bridget, though in real history, there is no evidence of a romantic or criminal involvement.

How the Series Portrays the Relationship with the Maid

In the series, Bridget Sullivan is depicted as a character who encourages Lizzie to commit the murders. In reality, there is no proof that the maid was an accomplice. Sullivan herself, who worked in Andrew and Abby Borden's home for nearly three years, stated after the murders that she was unhappy with the job, but stayed out of loyalty to Abby Borden.

The Historical Context Presented

The setting takes place in Fall River, Massachusetts, where the events occurred in a seemingly ordinary family home. The series illustrates family tensions, including disputes over property arrangements and potential abuses. The narrative also addresses speculation regarding Lizzie's sexuality, which has been a topic of debate ever since.

The Relevance of the Series Today

By retelling the case, the series highlights issues of gender and power, as well as the way the media treated Lizzie Borden at the time. The production also reflects on how the story continues to fascinate audiences while offering a critical view of the theories that have emerged over more than a century.

Conclusion on Ella Beatty's Performance

Ella Beatty delivers a performance that, according to critics, captures the complexity of Lizzie Borden, presenting a young woman facing family and social conflicts. The series remains faithful to the history while crafting a dramatic plot that keeps the audience engaged.

With information from The Guardian and Yahoo News UK.
